title: Soft Pull-Apart Milk Dinner Rolls
summary: A cooked water-and-flour paste is mixed with milk, egg, bread flour and yeast, enriched with butter, shaped into 12 balls in a round tin and baked to 88-90 °C.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the flour paste
steps.text: Whisk the water and 20 g flour over medium heat 1-2 minutes until thick and smooth. Whisk in the cold milk, then the egg.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the flour and yeast and mix until no dry flour remains. Rest 15 minutes.

steps.title: Knead in butter
steps.text: Add the sugar and salt and knead 5 minutes, then add the butter a little at a time and knead 5 minutes more.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave about 1 hour until doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide into 12 tight balls, arrange in the greased tin and prove 45-60 minutes until touching. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25-30 minutes until golden and 88-90 °C in the centre. Brush with butter and serve warm.

tips: The cooked paste makes a softer, longer-keeping roll.
Shape tight balls for even, round tops.
Weigh the pieces so they bake evenly.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature and eat within 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Refresh in a hot oven for a few minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
